correctness.rationale: For exact spoke set, each consecutive rim arc must omit at least one edge, giving a_d=x((1+x)^d-x^d). All optional spoke refinements are summed by U=A/(1-A), with coefficients x(lambda_+^d-lambda_-^d)/Delta. The cyclic logarithmic expansion recovers Z_n, yielding the exact all-subset inclusion law. Local limits and the AR(1) Toeplitz determinant show the DPP, whose Fourier symbol lies strictly between 0 and 1. Renewal probabilities are normalized by A(1/lambda_+)=1; differentiation gives mean Delta/x and their renewal mass yields the identical joint probabilities. Finite correlation follows from an explicit strict AM-GM inequality. Exact independent brute-force forest enumeration and rational Toeplitz determinant tests verify 822+1143 finite assertions, not infinite results.
risks: The natural infinite-volume process is only the spoke marginal; no claim about all wheel edges.
Finite enumeration cannot establish general identities, which are proved algebraically.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the all-positive-fugacity k-spoke inclusion law AND its explicit infinite-volume renewal/determinantal identification. Prior unit-fugacity wheel pair correlations and count are explicitly recognized as covered, not novel. Actual research-record queries and primary literature comparisons did not find an implication-equivalent stated process-level theorem; ladder spanning-tree DPP results are distinct. The uninspected full text of the very relevant multivariate wheel paper is a real remaining priority risk rather than proof of absence.
residual_risks: The complete paper behind doi:10.1016/j.spl.2026.110960 is inaccessible; its multivariate transfer derivation could imply the finite all-k spoke formula, even though the accessible abstract states only pairwise uniform results.
General older renewal, transfer-matrix or determinantal-process literature might contain an equivalent infinite-volume law under different terminology; searches cannot prove historical uniqueness.
The all-fugacity two-spoke inequality is a consequence of the new formula, but the known x=1 two-edge case is excluded from novelty.

value.rationale: A motivated model-specific process-level classification: the hub-spoke marginal of an unrooted random forest unexpectedly has a complete all-order exact law and becomes a stationary renewal process that is simultaneously determinantal. It gives a reproducible positive-fugacity family with explicit gap distribution, intensity, correlations and sharp geometric covariance decay. This is stronger structural information than finite enumeration or isolated pairwise inequalities, relevant to understanding local negative dependence in the arboreal gas.
risks: The graph family is specialized to wheel hub spokes; applications to other graph types remain unproved.
